title: Phased commit coordinator and preflight sandbox for VPC control plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a phased commit coordinator and an automated preflight sandbox to validate VPC/private control plane version promotions. The goal is to provide an automated safety harness that runs an isolated, short-lived control plane environment (preflight sandbox) per candidate release, runs deterministic acceptance suites and system-level probes, and produces a promotion decision (allow/hold/reject) consumed by the rollout controller. This reduces blast radius for private control plane upgrades and gives product and SRE teams high-confidence signals before tenant-facing promotions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Terraform module can provision an ephemeral sandbox control plane in an existing test VPC with the candidate control plane version and seeded tenant metadata

A2: The coordinator can run an automated acceptance suite (API contract checks, kv-cache smoke, leader-election probes, rolling-restart tolerance) and emit a clear pass/fail summary within configurable timeouts
A3: The coordinator exposes a promotion decision endpoint and a signed artifact that the rollout operator can consume to gate production promotions
A4: Sandbox teardown is automatic (configurable TTL) and leaves no residual infra or IAM bindings
A5: New telemetry dashboards (sandbox run success rate, time-to-verify, divergence ratios) are created in Console and linked to rollout run records
implementation_notes: High level approach: 1) Extend existing private IaC modules with an 'ephemeral_controlplane' flavor that uses versioned manifests and isolates operator RBAC to the sandbox namespace. 2) Implement a lightweight coordinator service (stateless controller) that: creates sandbox via Terraform Cloud runs or Terraform Runner, waits for control plane readiness, triggers acceptance test plan, collects metrics, and signs a promotion decision. 3) Acceptance tests are a mix of k6 synthetic traffic, contract tests (openapi checks), KV cache short-lived writes/reads across epochs, and operator lifecycle probes (simulate node drain, leader failover). 4) Provide an opt-in webhook for SRE/PM to review failures before automatic rejection. 5) Capture full artifacts: logs, diffs of rendered manifests, and test run artifacts in a release bucket for postmortem analysis.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge coordinator and IaC changes to canary branch and run internal sandbox against latest nightly build
Step 1: Run 3 successful sandbox validations consecutively (24h window) to establish baseline
Step 2: Trigger a 0.5% tenant traffic slice promotion using rollout operator with automated rollback rules
Step 3: Expand to 5% if SLI stable for 2 hours, then to 25% after 24 hours, then full promotion by release window
Step 4: If coordinator returns 'hold' at any stage, stop expansion and create incident-ticket with artifacts attached
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback via rollout operator to previous control plane version when SLI breach exceeds configured thresholds
If rollback fails, quarantine affected tenants and initiate manual failover playbook
Provision an emergency sandbox with previous version to validate rollback efficacy before re-promoting
notes: We must ensure the ephemeral sandbox does not leak IAM permissions into customer namespaces. Use least-privilege service account and enforce constrained service limit quotas. Coordinate with platform-security for an initial threat-model review. Also align with cost-controls to prevent runaway sandboxes during test loops.
dependencies_explained: ENG-12147 provides the version catalogue used to choose compatible operator/CRD pairs. ENG-70312 contains the rollback playbook and tenant quarantine steps. ENG-21456 defines phase gating primitives the rollout operator will call.
